target_customer: Mobile app developers and app companies that needed a fast on-device database, later enterprises needing mobile data sync
problem: SQLite and Core Data were slow, verbose and hard to use for mobile apps, costing developers many lines of code and weeks of work.
business_model: Open source mobile database, monetized through a paid Realm Mobile Platform for data synchronization and enterprise features

founders.name: Alexander Stigsen
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat (2015) describes both founders as former Nokia developers.

founders.name: Bjarne Christiansen
previous_startups: Cohera Inc (founded and led, per YC page bio)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists experience in industrial condition monitoring and mobile database technology.

competitors.name: SQLite
competitors.what: Default embedded database on Android and iOS

competitors.name: Core Data
competitors.what: Apple's object persistence framework for iOS

technical_complexity.rationale: A new database engine written in C++ from scratch with zero copy design and bindings for several languages and platforms, requiring deep systems engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Hard to build a new embedded database, and apps built on it were costly to migrate, but it was open source and the free core limited monetization.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform owners kept SQLite and Core Data. Couchbase Mobile arrived as an alternative. MongoDB bought Realm in April 2019 and later announced the end of the Realm sync service, with shutdown set for September 2025 per secondary sources.

market_need_then: Mobile developers widely complained about SQLite and Core Data boilerplate and speed. By March 2015 VentureBeat listed BuzzFeed, Expensify, Groupon, Intuit and Rite Aid as customers.

branding.domain_note: Moved from tightdb.com to realm.io; realm.io now redirects to MongoDB docs.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused, pitch of replacing SQLite and Core Data

rebrands.why: Product renamed on public release; the reason is not stated in sources
MongoDB rebrand after the acquisition, per a single encyclopedia source

branding.community_and_virality: Open source project with a large developer community and conference talks; no sourced evidence of merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among iOS and Android developers as an open source database, but a developer tools brand without wider consumer reach.

pivots.to: Realm Mobile Platform with a paid data synchronization service
pivots.why: Needed a monetization path beyond the free database; date and wording are not confirmed by an opened source

outcome_analysis: Realm replaced SQLite and Core Data for many apps through a faster open source engine and grew to well known customers, raising a $20 million round led by Khosla in 2015. Monetizing a free database proved hard, and MongoDB bought it for about $39 million in cash in April 2019, a modest price versus the roughly $29 million to $42 million raised.
notes: VentureBeat said Realm had raised $29M to date as of March 2015 (unclear whether including the $20M); earlier rounds not itemized. Dataconomy labeled the $20M as Series B while VentureBeat does not name a series; stage recorded as series_a is therefore uncertain and should be read as other if strict. Series B of about $11.2M in August 2018 and Ericsson Ventures investment in September 2017 appear in aggregator or blocked sources (the Business Wire release returned HTTP 403) and are unverified, not recorded as rounds. Final merger price reported as $38.8M after adjustments. Competitors listed are the status quo options; no dated 2011 competitor coverage was found. Pivot entry is a loose description.
